rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'a sibling worktree' (chunk 1 line 21) defines itself in-sentence, reused unproblematically at chunks 2-4. 'the second session' (chunk 2 line 44) resolves against chunk 0 line 7 ('open a second session there'). 'the sibling worktree directory Claude just named' (chunk 3 line 48) resolves against chunk 2's claim one chunk prior. 'this window'/'here' (chunk 3 line 56) resolve against chunk 3's own header. The one term with no in-file antecedent, 'the compound step' (chunk 3 line 56, 'back in the main lane where the compound step lives'), is arc-earned spine vocabulary, not a fresh forward-pointing referent: 'compound' is named and taught as a concrete move at M1 (getting-going.md 'the loop is orient -> fix -> compound -> close'; exercises/compound-and-close.md 'the compound step (plan -> work -> review -> compound, Kieran Klaassen's loop)'), reused at M2 (plan-mode-done-right.md), and reused again inside this same module at earn-the-trust.md's 'Sharpen the skill from evidence' section ('the compound runs here'). Per the carve-out, training-named artifacts earned in a prior module don't re-earn per file/slide. No other pronoun or demonstrative in any chunk lacks an in-chunk or prior-chunk antecedent.

Chunk 3 line 56 ('the evidence-based sharpen runs later still, back in the main lane where the compound step lives') names no file by position; it locates a later beat by window and by claim (main lane, the compound step), not by 'the next exercise said' phrasing. Verified against earn-the-trust.md's actual sequencing: this exercise (module opener) precedes Map the access surface, Threat-model with STRIDE, Author your test-strategy skill, and the module-level 'Sharpen the skill from evidence' section runs after all four, back in m3-security. The one file-title link (chunk 1 line 21, Multi-session and Git survival guide) points at a real document location by title -- navigational-pointer carve-out. Chunk 4 line 75 ('Module 3's exercises name which window the work runs in') is a generic forward-looking claim, verified true against map-the-access-surface.md, threat-model-with-stride.md, and author-test-strategy-skill.md, each of which opens with its own Window: callout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 3 line 48's backward pointer resolves against chunk 2, one chunk prior -- exists, in order. The two forward claims in chunk 3 line 56 were checked against the beats they promise: 'a separate step that revisits this window's scrollback' matches earn-the-trust.md's m3-quality scrollback-grab instruction inside 'Sharpen the skill from evidence'; 'the evidence-based sharpen ... where the compound step lives' matches that same section's prompt fence and its own 'the compound runs here' text. Both referenced beats exist in the module's current file set.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess/predict-before-reveal instruction anywhere in the body.

Chunk 2 is the thinnest slide (one bullet) but carries a self-standing claim -- 'Claude reports the sibling worktree path. That path is where the second session opens.' -- not a bare wait-state bullet.

Checked all sub-items across all 5 chunks: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlatives; no number-with-own-retraction; no abstraction-noun stacks; no verb triplets with an empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, or Connections-as-proper-noun in the body (grepped clean). 'The compound step' (chunk 3 line 56) reads as maintainer shorthand at first glance but is the training's own taught vocabulary, not repo-authoring dialect: students perform 'the compound step' themselves starting at M1 (compound-and-close.md); it is never used here as an authoring/process term about the curriculum itself. 'Main quest'/'side-quest'/'lane' are this exercise's own defined narrative device (established in its own chunk 0), meant for the student to use, not maintainer jargon.
